title: Introduce priority-aware graceful-ejection + credit-based admission to reduce hosted GPU queue build-up
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: During the 2026-03-09 hosted API capacity event we observed sustained GPU queue growth across several regions that resulted in elevated p95/p99 generation latencies and request throttling. Root cause analysis shows three concurrent contributors: (1) a spike in long-context batch requests from a single large customer, (2) an autoscaler configuration that delayed pod provisioning under bursty spike patterns, and (3) the admission controller defaulting to FIFO admission without respecting tiered priorities. This ticket implements a two-stage mitigation: (A) immediate runtime changes to apply credit-based admission per customer + graceful-ejection rules that preferentially drop/fast-fail low-priority work before it amplifies queue depth, and (B) medium-term autoscaler and pre-warm policies to reduce provisioning lag for bursty workloads.
acceptance_criteria: New admission controller rejects or fast-fails low-priority/low-SLO requests when per-customer credit exhausted and preserves tokens for high-priority traffic (test harness with synthetic workload shows 30% reduction in p99 queue depth compared to baseline)

Graceful-ejection path implemented: ability to terminate queued requests with a structured error + telemetry tag so SDKs/clients can fallback; system shows <1% false-positive ejections in canary region
Autoscaler pre-warm policy landed and rollouts tuned so median pod provision time under synthetic burst drops from 22s to <8s
Dashboards and alerts updated: new GPU queue-depth by customer tier, admission-credit-burn-rate, and ejection-rate charts; SLOs for API p95/p99 validated against synthetic replay
Runbook updated with playbook entries for manual credit adjustments, emergency reserve pool activation, and post-incident troubleshooting steps
tasks: Design and prototype credit-based admission controller (Marcus) - create PR and benchmark in staging
Implement graceful-ejection path in runtime with structured error payload (Aisha + Priya) - include SDK guidance
Autoscaler tuning: implement pre-warm/reserve pools and faster provisioning profile (Jorge) - integrate with k8s-provisioner
Canary rollout to two low-traffic regions and A/B synthetic load test (QA - Elena)
Update Console dashboards and create alert rules (Observability - Tian)
Write runbook additions and postmortem section describing triggers and mitigations (Operations - Noah)
notes: Immediate mitigation executed at 2026-03-10 03:12 UTC: temporarily increased high-priority token bucket for existing enterprise customers and enabled conservative queue-time cap (results: 18% drop in p99 across affected clusters).
Root cause threads: spike came from a scheduled data-replay job in customer 'OrchidAI' that used long-sequence generation with large batch sizes; customer-side mitigation coordinated via SEs.

Autoscaler review: current aggressive cooldowns and scaleDownThreshold were preventing quick scale-up during repeated spikes; proposed change reduces stabilizationWindow from 60s->10s for scaleUp events only.

Design trade-offs discussed: strict per-request fast-fail reduces tail but increases client error surface; we will ship fast-fail with clear structured error codes and SDK retry guidance to avoid UX regressions.
